metadata.title: A Stochastic Gradient Method with an Exponential Convergence Rate for Finite Training Sets
metadata.authors: Nicolas Le Roux, Mark Schmidt, Francis Bach

nodes.name: Finite-sum strongly-convex minimization
nodes.statement: Minimize a finite sample average of smooth functions: $\minimize{x\in\mathbb{R}^p} g(x) \defd \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)$, with each $f_i$ smooth and $g$ strongly convex.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the average of $n$ smooth functions where the average is strongly convex.

nodes.name: $\ell_2$-regularized empirical risk minimization
nodes.statement: $\minimize{x\in\mathbb{R}^p} \frac{\lambda}{2}\|x\|^2 + \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n l_i(x)$, with convex smooth losses $l_i$ and regularization $\lambda$.

nodes.name: $\ell_2$-regularized logistic regression
nodes.statement: Special case of $\ell_2$-regularized ERM with $f_i(x) \defd \frac{\lambda}{2}\|x\|^2 + \log(1+\exp(-b_i a_i^T x))$ for binary labels $b_i \in \{-1,1\}$.

nodes.name: $\ell_2$-regularized least squares
nodes.statement: $\minimize{x\in\mathbb{R}^p} \frac{\lambda}{2}\|x\|^2 + \frac{1}{2n}\|Ax-b\|^2$, with Fenchel dual $\minimize{y\in\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{n}{2}\|y\|^2 + \frac{1}{2\lambda}y^\top AA^\top y + y^\top b$.

nodes.name: Lipschitz-continuous gradient
nodes.statement: Each $f_i'$ is $L$-Lipschitz: $\|f_i'(x)-f_i'(y)\| \leq L\|x-y\|$ for all $x,y \in \mathbb{R}^p$.

nodes.name: Strong convexity (constant $\mu$)
nodes.statement: $g = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i f_i$ is $\mu$-strongly convex: $x \mapsto g(x) - \frac{\mu}{2}\|x\|^2$ is convex (with $\mu > 0$).

nodes.name: Variance of gradients at the optimum
nodes.statement: $\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \|f_i'(x^\ast)\|^2$, where $x^\ast$ is the unique minimizer of $g$.

nodes.name: Memory vector $y_i^k$
nodes.statement: $y_i^k = f_i'(x^k)$ if $i=i_k$ and $y_i^k = y_i^{k-1}$ otherwise; stores the most recent gradient evaluation of each $f_i$.

nodes.name: Lyapunov state vector $\theta^k$
nodes.section: Appendix A.1 Problem set-up and notations
nodes.statement: $\theta^k = (y_1^k, \dots, y_n^k, x^k)^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{(n+1)p}$ and $\theta^\ast = (f_1'(x^\ast), \dots, f_n'(x^\ast), x^\ast)^\top$.

nodes.name: Selection function $S(j, i_{1:k})$
nodes.statement: $S(j, i_{1:k}) = 1/n$ if $j$ corresponds to the last iteration where $j = i_k$, and $0$ otherwise; gives the SAG re-write $x^{k+1} = x^k - \sum_{j=1}^k \alpha_k S(j, i_{1:k}) f_{i_j}'(x^j)$.

nodes.name: Full gradient (FG) iteration
nodes.statement: $x^{k+1} = x^k - \alpha_k g'(x^k) = x^k - \frac{\alpha_k}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i'(x^k)$.

nodes.name: Stochastic gradient (SG) iteration
nodes.statement: $x^{k+1} = x^k - \alpha_k f_{i_k}'(x^k)$, with $i_k$ sampled uniformly from $\{1,\dots,n\}$.

nodes.name: Stochastic average gradient (SAG) iteration
nodes.statement: $x^{k+1} = x^k - \frac{\alpha_k}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n y_i^k$, where $y_i^k$ stores the most recent gradient $f_i'$ evaluated at the iterate when $i$ was last sampled.

nodes.name: $\ell_2$ exact-regularizer recursion
nodes.statement: $d \leftarrow d - y_i;\; y_i \leftarrow l_i'(x^k);\; d \leftarrow d + y_i;\; x \leftarrow (1-\alpha\lambda)x - \frac{\alpha}{m}d$.

nodes.name: Standing assumptions (Section 3)
nodes.statement: (A1) Each $f_i$ is differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient. (A2) $g = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i f_i$ is $\mu$-strongly convex with $\mu>0$. (A3) Initialize $y_i^0 = 0$ for all $i$.

nodes.name: Stochastic Average Gradient (SAG)
nodes.statement: Randomized incremental method that maintains a memory of the most recent gradient $y_i^k$ for each $f_i$ and updates $x^{k+1} = x^k - \frac{\alpha_k}{n}\sum_i y_i^k$.
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize $y_i^0=0$ for $i=1..n$; for $k=1,2,\dots$: sample $i_k \sim \mathrm{Unif}\{1,..,n\}$; set $y_{i_k}^k \leftarrow f_{i_k}'(x^{k-1})$ and $y_i^k \leftarrow y_i^{k-1}$ for $i\neq i_k$; update $x^k \leftarrow x^{k-1} - \frac{\alpha}{n}\sum_i y_i^k$.

nodes.name: SAG with line search (SAG-LS)
nodes.statement: Practical SAG variant using step size $\alpha_k = 2/(L_k + n\lambda)$ with adaptive $L_k$ from a line search that doubles $L_k$ when the local Lipschitz inequality fails and multiplies by $2^{-1/n}$ each iteration.
output: Iterates $x^k$ converging to $x^\ast$ with adaptive step size

nodes.name: Full Gradient (FG) method
nodes.statement: Cauchy's gradient descent: $x^{k+1} = x^k - \alpha_k g'(x^k)$ with cost $O(np)$ per step and linear rate $O(\rho^k)$ depending on the condition number of $g$.

nodes.name: Stochastic Gradient (SG) method
nodes.statement: Robbins--Monro iteration $x^{k+1} = x^k - \alpha_k f_{i_k}'(x^k)$ with sublinear $O(1/k)$ rate under suitable decreasing step sizes.

nodes.name: Incremental Aggregated Gradient (IAG)
nodes.statement: Identical recursion to SAG~\eqref{eq:SAG} but with a cyclic (deterministic) choice of $i_k$ rather than uniform sampling.

nodes.name: Accelerated Full Gradient (AFG)
nodes.statement: Nesterov's accelerated FG method interleaving gradient steps with an extrapolation; achieves rate $1-\sqrt{\mu/L}$ in the strongly-convex case.

nodes.name: Pegasos
nodes.statement: State-of-the-art SG method using step size $\alpha_k = 1/(\mu k)$ with a projection onto a norm-ball containing $x^\ast$.

nodes.name: Regularized Dual Averaging (RDA)
nodes.statement: Sample-average SG method based on dual averaging, used as a state-of-the-art baseline.

nodes.name: Epoch SG (ESG)
nodes.statement: Epoch-based SG with constant step size and averaging within each epoch; optimal for non-smooth strongly-convex stochastic optimization.

nodes.name: Nearly-Optimal SG (NOSG)
nodes.statement: Combines ideas from SG and AFG to obtain near-optimal dependency on problem-dependent constants.

nodes.name: L-BFGS
nodes.statement: Limited-memory quasi-Newton method tuned for log-linear models; used as a strong full-batch baseline.

nodes.name: Convergence of SAG with small step size $\alpha = 1/(2nL)$
nodes.statement: With constant step size $\alpha_k = \frac{1}{2nL}$, the SAG iterates satisfy for $k \geq 1$: $\mathbb{E}\|x^k - x^\ast\|^2 \leq (1 - \frac{\mu}{8Ln})^k [3\|x^0 - x^\ast\|^2 + \frac{9\sigma^2}{4L^2}]$.

nodes.name: Convergence of SAG with large step size $\alpha = 1/(2n\mu)$
nodes.statement: If $n \geq \frac{8L}{\mu}$, with step size $\alpha_k = \frac{1}{2n\mu}$ the SAG iterates satisfy for $k \geq n$: $\mathbb{E}[g(x^k) - g(x^\ast)] \leq C(1 - \frac{1}{8n})^k$, where $C = \frac{16L}{3n}\|x^0-x^\ast\|^2 + \frac{4\sigma^2}{3n\mu}(8\log(1+\frac{\mu n}{4L}) + 1)$.
assumptions: First $n$ iterations are SG; SAG initialized with the average of these iterates and $y_i^0=0$

nodes.name: Recursion for the quadratic Lyapunov term
nodes.statement: For $P = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} A & b \\ b^\top & c \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, the conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}[(\theta^k-\theta^\ast)^\top P (\theta^k-\theta^\ast)\mid \mathcal{F}_{k-1}]$ admits an explicit closed form in terms of $\theta^{k-1}$ and the auxiliary matrix $S = A - \frac{\alpha}{n} b e^\top - \frac{\alpha}{n} e b^\top + \frac{\alpha^2}{n^2} e c e^\top$.
assumptions: SAG recursion for $\theta^k$ as in Appendix A.1
conclusions: Closed form in $y^{k-1} - f'(x^\ast)$, $f'(x^{k-1}) - f'(x^\ast)$, and $x^{k-1} - x^\ast$ involving $S$ and $\Diag(\diag(S))$

nodes.name: SG bound used to initialize SAG
nodes.section: Appendix A.3 Convergence results for SGD
nodes.statement: With $\gamma_k = \frac{1}{2L + \mu k/2}$, averaging gives $\mathbb{E} g\bigl(\frac{1}{k}\sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \tilde{x}^i\bigr) - g(x^\ast) \leq \frac{2L}{k}\|x^0 - x^\ast\|^2 + \frac{4\sigma^2}{k\mu}\log(1+\frac{\mu k}{4L})$.
assumptions: SG recursion $\tilde{x}^k = \tilde{x}^{k-1} - \gamma_k f_{i_k}'(\tilde{x}^{k-1})$ with step $\gamma_k = 1/(2L + \mu k/2)$

nodes.name: Lower bound for first-order strongly-convex stochastic optimization
nodes.statement: Under unbiased gradient access, the rate $\mathbb{E}[g(x^k)] - g(x^\ast) = O(1/k)$ is optimal for strongly-convex stochastic optimization; no algorithm relying only on unbiased gradient measurements can do better.
nodes.origin_citation: Nemirovsky & Yudin 1983; Nemirovski et al. 2009; Agarwal et al. 2010
assumptions: Algorithm accesses $g$ only via unbiased measurements of objective and gradient

nodes.name: FG linear convergence (Nesterov)
nodes.statement: With a constant step size, the FG method satisfies $g(x^k) - g(x^\ast) = O(\rho^k)$ for some $\rho<1$ depending on the condition number of $g$.
assumptions: FG iteration with constant step size

nodes.name: Co-coercivity of Lipschitz gradients
nodes.statement: For each $i$, $\|f_i'(x) - f_i'(x^\ast)\|^2 \leq L (f_i'(x) - f_i'(x^\ast))^\top (x - x^\ast)$, and summing $\sum_i \|f_i'(x^{k-1}) - f_i'(x^\ast)\|^2 \leq nL\, g'(x^{k-1})^\top (x^{k-1}-x^\ast)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1 ($\alpha = 1/(2nL)$)
nodes.statement: Construct a quadratic Lyapunov $Q(\theta^k) = (\theta^k - \theta^\ast)^\top P (\theta^k-\theta^\ast)$ with explicit $A,b,c$, show linear contraction $\mathbb{E} Q(\theta^k) \leq (1-\delta)\mathbb{E} Q(\theta^{k-1})$ with $\delta = \mu/(8nL)$, then dominate $\|x^k-x^\ast\|^2$ by $3 Q(\theta^k)$ via a Schur-complement argument.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2 ($\alpha = 1/(2n\mu)$)
nodes.statement: Use Lyapunov $Q(\theta^k) = 2g(x^k + \frac{\alpha}{n}e^\top y^k) - 2g(x^\ast) + (\theta^k-\theta^\ast)^\top P (\theta^k-\theta^\ast)$, prove linear contraction with rate $1 - 1/(8n)$ when $n\mu/L \geq 8$, dominate $g(x^k) - g(x^\ast)$ by $Q$, then absorb the SG initialization phase.

nodes.name: Define quadratic Lyapunov $Q(\theta^k)$
nodes.statement: Set $Q(\theta^k) = (\theta^k - \theta^\ast)^\top P (\theta^k - \theta^\ast)$ with $A = 3n\alpha^2 I + \frac{\alpha^2}{n}(\frac{1}{n}-2)ee^\top$, $b = -\alpha(1-\frac{1}{n})e$, $c = I$, giving $S = 3n\alpha^2 I$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma A.4 to get recursion for $\mathbb{E} Q$
nodes.statement: Plug the chosen $A,b,c$ into the recursion of Lemma A.4 (LP258.1) to express $\mathbb{E}[Q(\theta^k)\mid\mathcal{F}_{k-1}]$ in terms of $y^{k-1}-f'(x^\ast)$, $f'(x^{k-1})-f'(x^\ast)$, and $x^{k-1}-x^\ast$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|f'(x^{k-1})-f'(x^\ast)\|^2$ by Lipschitz
nodes.statement: Use $(f'(x^{k-1})-f'(x^\ast))^\top (f'(x^{k-1})-f'(x^\ast)) \leq nL\, g'(x^{k-1})^\top (x^{k-1}-x^\ast)$ from Nesterov Theorem 2.1.5.

nodes.name: Eliminate cross term via completing the square
nodes.statement: For symmetric negative-definite $M$, use $s^\top M s + s^\top t \leq -\frac{1}{4} t^\top M^{-1} t$ to remove the $(y^{k-1}-f'(x^\ast))^\top e (x^{k-1}-x^\ast)$ cross term, yielding $-\frac{\delta^2(1-1/n)^2 n}{3n\delta - 1 - 2\delta + (\delta-1)/n}\|x^{k-1}-x^\ast\|^2$.

nodes.name: Pick $\delta = \mu/(8nL)$ and verify positivity
nodes.statement: With $\delta = \mu/(8nL)$ and $\alpha = 1/(2nL)$, verify $2\alpha - 3\alpha^2 nL + \frac{\delta^2(1-1/n)^2 n}{3n\delta - 1 - 2\delta + (\delta-1)/n}\frac{1}{\mu} - \frac{\delta}{\mu} \geq 0$, hence $\mathbb{E}[Q(\theta^k)\mid\mathcal{F}_{k-1}] \leq (1-\delta)Q(\theta^{k-1})$.

nodes.name: Iterate to linear convergence of $\mathbb{E} Q(\theta^k)$
nodes.statement: Take total expectation and unroll: $\mathbb{E} Q(\theta^k) \leq (1 - \frac{\mu}{8nL})^k Q(\theta^0)$.

nodes.name: Domination $Q(\theta^k) \geq \tfrac{1}{3}\|x^k-x^\ast\|^2$ via Schur complement
nodes.statement: Show $\frac{2}{3} I - b^\top A^{-1} b \succ 0$ for $n\geq 2$ so that $P - \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & I/3 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr) \succ 0$, hence $\|x^k-x^\ast\|^2 \leq 3 Q(\theta^k)$.

nodes.name: Initial value $Q(\theta^0)$ with $y_i^0 = 0$
nodes.statement: With $y_i^0 = 0$: $Q(\theta^0) = \frac{3\sigma^2}{4L^2} + \|x^0-x^\ast\|^2$, yielding the final bound $\mathbb{E}\|x^k-x^\ast\|^2 \leq (1-\frac{\mu}{8nL})^k(\frac{9\sigma^2}{4L^2} + 3\|x^0-x^\ast\|^2)$.

nodes.name: Define enriched Lyapunov $Q(\theta^k)$
nodes.statement: Set $Q(\theta^k) = 2g(x^k + \frac{\alpha}{n}e^\top y^k) - 2g(x^\ast) + (\theta^k-\theta^\ast)^\top P (\theta^k-\theta^\ast)$ with $A = \frac{\eta\alpha}{n}I + \frac{\alpha}{n}(1-2\nu)ee^\top$, $b = -\nu e$, $c = 0$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma A.4 and convexity to bound $\mathbb{E} Q$ recursion
nodes.statement: Plug $A,b,c$ into Lemma A.4 (LP258.1) and use the convexity inequality $g(x^{k-1} + \frac{\alpha}{n}e^\top y^{k-1}) \geq g(x^{k-1}) + \frac{\alpha}{n}g'(x^{k-1})^\top e^\top y^{k-1}$.

nodes.name: Complete the square in $y^{k-1}-f'(x^\ast)$
nodes.statement: With $\tau_{y,I},\tau_{y,e}<0$, complete the square to bound the quadratic form by a single $-(x^{k-1}-x^\ast)^\top g'(x^{k-1})$ term plus a $\|g'(x^{k-1})\|^2$ term.

nodes.name: Substitute $\delta = 1/(8n)$, $\nu=1/(2n)$, $\eta=2$, $\alpha = 1/(2n\mu)$
nodes.statement: With these choices and $n\mu/L\geq 8$, the coefficient of $(x^{k-1}-x^\ast)^\top g'(x^{k-1})$ is $\leq 0$ and the coefficient of $\|g'(x^{k-1})\|^2$ is $\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Iterate to $\mathbb{E} Q(\theta^k) \leq (1-1/(8n))^k Q(\theta^0)$
nodes.statement: Take expectation and unroll: $\mathbb{E} Q(\theta^k) \leq (1 - 1/(8n))^k [2(g(x^0) - g(x^\ast)) + \sigma^2/(n\mu)]$.

nodes.name: Domination $Q(\theta^k) \geq \tfrac{6}{7}(g(x^k)-g(x^\ast))$
nodes.statement: Minimize the lower bound over $e^\top y^k$, then use $\mu/L \geq 8/n$ and Lipschitz of $g'$ to obtain $Q(\theta^k) \geq \frac{6}{7}(g(x^k)-g(x^\ast))$.

nodes.name: Initialize via $n$ SG iterations
nodes.statement: Use Lemma LP258.2 (SG averaging) to bound $\mathbb{E} g(x^n) - g(x^\ast)$, and combine with the SAG contraction to obtain the final bound for $k\geq n$.

nodes.name: Initialize $y_i^0 = 0$ for all $i$
nodes.statement: Set $y_i^0 \leftarrow 0$ for $i=1,\dots,n$ and choose initial iterate $x^0$.

nodes.name: Sample index $i_k$ uniformly
nodes.statement: Pick $i_k \sim \mathrm{Uniform}\{1,\dots,n\}$ at each iteration $k$.

nodes.name: Update memory $y^k_{i_k}$
nodes.statement: Set $y^k_{i_k} \leftarrow f_{i_k}'(x^{k-1})$ and $y^k_i \leftarrow y^{k-1}_i$ for $i \neq i_k$.

nodes.name: Iterate update $x^k$
nodes.statement: Set $x^k \leftarrow x^{k-1} - \frac{\alpha}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n y_i^k$ (in practice divide by $m$, the number of distinct sampled indices, to mitigate bias).

nodes.name: Initialize $L_0 = 1$
nodes.statement: Set $L_0 \leftarrow 1$ and $\alpha_0 \leftarrow 2/(L_0 + n\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Line-search test to update $L_k$
nodes.statement: If $\|f_{i_k}'(x^k)\|^2 > 10^{-8}$ and $f_{i_k}(x^k - (1/L_k)f_{i_k}'(x^k)) > f_{i_k}(x^k) - \frac{1}{2L_k}\|f_{i_k}'(x^k)\|^2$, double $L_k \leftarrow 2 L_k$; else multiply $L_k \leftarrow 2^{-1/n} L_k$.

nodes.name: SAG update with adaptive step
nodes.statement: Apply the SAG update~\eqref{eq:SAG} with step size $\alpha_k = 2/(L_k + n\lambda)$.

nodes.name: $\ell_2$-regularized logistic regression on benchmark data
nodes.statement: Numerical comparison of SAG (with constant Lipschitz step and with line-search) against FG, AFG, L-BFGS, Pegasos, RDA, ESG, NOSG on the binary classification datasets quantum, protein, sido, rcv1, and covertype with $\lambda = 1/n$.

nodes.name: Hand-tuned step-size comparison
nodes.statement: Second experiment: FG, AFG, Pegasos, SG, ASG (averaged SG), IAG and SAG, each with the best step size in hindsight (powers of 10), on the same five datasets.

nodes.name: Numerical illustration: SAG rate vs FG/AFG
SAG matches the SG $O(1/k)$ rate
nodes.statement: Since $(1-\mu/(8Ln))^k \leq \exp(-k\mu/(8Ln)) \leq 8Ln/(k\mu) = O(n/k)$, the small-step SAG iteration also achieves the standard SG rate, albeit with a constant proportional to $n$.

nodes.name: Step size $1/(16L)$ recovers Proposition 2 rate
nodes.statement: Since Proposition 2 holds for any $\mu \geq 8L/n$, taking $\mu = 8L/n$ shows that step size $\alpha_k = 1/(16L)$ achieves the same rate without explicit knowledge of $\mu$.

nodes.name: Conjectured faster rate for $\alpha_k = 1/L$
nodes.statement: Empirically $\alpha_k = 1/L$ and $\alpha_k = 2/(L+n\mu)$ work even when the Proposition 2 hypothesis fails; the authors conjecture rates substantially faster than Proposition 1 in the general case.

nodes.name: Termination criterion via memory norm
nodes.statement: The quantity $(1/n)\|\sum_i y_i^k\|$ converges to $\|g'(x^k)\|$ as $\|x^k - x^{k-1}\|\to 0$, providing a natural stopping criterion for SAG.
